open_obligations: Check that book summarisation is beyond what a single human could evaluate in the relevant sense.
Note that only about 5% of summaries match human quality, so the demonstration is partial.
Confirm that Wu et al. use human feedback at every level rather than only at leaves.
out.other_title: Can Iterated Amplification be applied to complex real-world beyond-human-scale tasks?
out.rationale: Christiano et al. leave open whether Iterated Amplification can be applied to complex real-world tasks. Wu et al. combine human feedback with recursive task decomposition to summarise whole books, report labelers could supervise without reading whole books, and find summaries match human quality in about 5% of books; the decomposition is fixed chunking rather than learned, and the task is not beyond human scale.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether recursive decomposition with human feedback can be applied to real tasks humans cannot easily evaluate directly, for whole-book summarisation

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The paper combines learning from human feedback with recursive task decomposition, using models trained on smaller parts of the task to help humans give feedback on the broader task; GPT-3 is fine-tuned with behavioural cloning and reward modeling to summarise small sections and then recursively summarise those summaries. The authors report labelers could supervise and evaluate quickly without reading whole books, and that the resulting summaries are sensible and match human-written quality in a few cases (about 5% of books).
title: Recursive task decomposition plus human feedback for summarizing entire books
